entities.summary:
Alexander Aetolus was a Hellenistic Greek poet and grammarian who worked at the Library of Alexandria, composing poetry in various genres, now largely lost. He is the only known Aetolian poet of antiquity.

Aetolus was born into a prominent Aetolian family in the 4th century BCE and received a classical education at the Library of Alexandria. His poetry reflects the diverse cultural influences of the time, including Egyptian, Greek, and Persian themes.

Despite the passing of centuries, Aetolus's work has left a lasting impact on the study of Hellenistic poetry and the development of Greek grammar. His legacy can be seen in the works of later poets, such as Callimachus and Theocritus, who drew upon his innovations in style and form.

One of the most striking aspects of Aetolus's poetry is its use of mythological themes, which were particularly popular in the Hellenistic period. His most famous work, the 'Aetolian Hymns,' is a collection of elegies that explore the mythology of the Aetolian region and its connections to the wider Greek world.

Today, Aetolus is recognized as a key figure in the history of Greek literature, and his poetry continues to be studied and appreciated by scholars and enthusiasts alike.
